title: strength
description: Per-exercise progression plus monthly tonnage, each with the fact that qualifies it. Tonnage is VOLUME, not strength: it falls when pull work gives way to isolation whatever happened to capacity, so the figure that answers "am I getting stronger" is each repeated exercise's working weight over time. The engine publishes numbers only — whether a trend is good is the coach's sentence to write (ADR 0012).

exercises.description: One entry per exercise name the parsed sets contain, exact-name matched (Twisting Curl and Zottman Curl are distinct movements; nothing fuzzy). Points are per DAY: the heaviest weight one rep moved that day, and the day's summed kg·reps for the exercise — two numbers because when the weight drops and the reps rise, the product is the only one that says whether work went up.

monthly.description: Every strength month from strength_coverage, INCLUDING the months the career spine refuses — a table can qualify a number where a curve cannot. `known` is the both-possible flag (ADR 0009): 0 means the month sits under the coverage bar and no tonnage is claimed for it (kg is 0 there, an impossible-zero behind the flag), 1 means kg is the month's summed lifted mass. covered/total is the denominator that keeps a coverage shift from reading as a training trend.

sessions.description: The gaps themselves, made visible: with_sets parsed into rows; pasted_unparsed carried a non-empty description that yielded nothing (a format stride does not read — a different fact from never pasted); the remainder of total never had a paste to read. Deliberate omissions are omissions the report can name because these counts exist.
